title: Choose the visual world for Sudoku
question: The roll assigned The Wall Chart. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Wall Chart
options.lineage: the laboratory reference chart pinned to a classroom wall
options.thesis: The board is not a card on a page — it is one large printed reference plate, and every control is chart apparatus printed onto it.
materials: flat process ink on coated chart stock
options.viewport: A full-bleed plate: a black masthead band across the top carrying the title in expanded gothic caps, the edition line, the difficulty selector printed as a tab strip and the elapsed counter as a printed readout; beneath it the 81 cells at wall scale, nine boxes tinted as ink families, lettered index tabs A-I across the top and 1-9 down the side; a state key column at the right; a NOTES band typeset along the foot.
options.risk: Nine tinted colour fields behind 81 numerals is a contrast tightrope — past roughly 12% ink the digits lose their footing, and the box structure must be carried by keyline weight too, never by colour alone.

raised.raise: SUBSTRATE: the sheet is a printed object, not a flat digital fill — halftone tint, paper tooth, and a half-pixel colour offset on the heavy rules where the plates did not quite register.
EMPTY IS AUTHORED: an unfilled cell is never blank. It carries its own faint printed coordinate in the corner, the way an unfilled row on a real chart still shows its ruling.

STATE PRINTS ITSELF: no floating toolbar anywhere. Difficulty, clue census, conflict count, elapsed time and every message are typeset into the chart's own masthead, key column and notes band as chart data.
ONE AXIS: masthead, plate and notes band all lock to a single governing centre axis, so the sheet reads as one composition at any width instead of a stack of panels.

regions.label: masthead: title, edition, difficulty tabs, clock

options.label: The Solver Trace
options.lineage: constraint-solver instrumentation: search trees, propagation logs, candidate bitmask tables
options.thesis: Show the mechanism that actually makes this product true — the backtracking search and its uniqueness proof — running beside the board you are playing.
options.viewport: A dense instrument document: search-tree rail down the left, the grid mid-page with live candidate counts inside every empty cell, a bitmask table down the right, and a propagation log running along the foot.
options.risk: This is exactly where a run aimed at an engineering audience predictably lands, and it reads as a debugger — which quietly narrows a page meant for anyone down to people who already like solvers.

options.label: Brick Build Instructions
options.thesis: Sky-blue page, keyline ink, oversized numerals and wordless arrows — prior work ghosts back, the piece you just placed arrives bright.
options.viewport: A sky-blue spread ruled to a stud module, the grid as the assembly, given clues ghosted and entered digits arriving bright with an arrow to their seat.
options.case: Wins audience identification outright — everyone has sat on a carpet with one of these, and ghosted-prior vs bright-new is exactly sudoku's given-vs-entered distinction. Loses product clarity: its governing grammar is numbered sequence, and sudoku has no step order, so the arrows and step numerals would teach an order that does not exist.
options.risk: Strip out the sequence and you have removed half the system's grammar; leave it in and the interface lies about the task.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: The content of this product is 81 numerals, so set it as a living specimen: enormous figures, hairline monospace labels, hierarchy by scale contrast alone.
options.viewport: The grid set as a glyph specimen at enormous size against tiny monospace labels, the timer and census as live coordinate readouts.
options.case: Holds product clarity brilliantly — huge numerals on a strict baseline grid is the most legible thing on this table, and digits genuinely are the content. Loses audience identification: specimen culture belongs to designers, so the page reads as a type artifact rather than a game a stranger would start playing.
options.risk: Generous negative space and no ornament leaves the board with nothing to stand on; done timidly it becomes the clean white card this redesign exists to escape.

options.label: Greiman Hybrid Collage
options.lineage: April Greiman hybrid poster, coarse bitmap at wall scale
options.thesis: The page as one deep collage of angled, ghosted layers you lift to the top of the stack.
options.viewport: Angled ramps of type over ghosted overlapping layers, magenta marking the live one.
options.case: Loses both axes. Puzzle players do not live in 1980s hybrid-poster culture, and ghosted overlapping layers set at an angle over a 9x9 of numerals destroys the scanning the whole task depends on.
options.kept: Accepting the substrate's own texture as a full-scale material rather than a decorative overlay.
options.risk: Rotation and transparency are the two things a scanned grid cannot survive.

options.label: Chaekgeori Reverse Perspective
options.lineage: painted scholar's-shelf screens built in reverse perspective
options.thesis: Nine boxes as painted shelf compartments whose far edges are wider than their near ones, opening toward you.
options.viewport: A cabinet of nine compartments widening as it deepens, each holding its filled digits as inventory.
options.case: Loses both axes. The cultural distance is total for a general audience, and reverse perspective makes cells physically unequal in size, which breaks the uniform scan a 9x9 is entirely built on.
options.kept: Every compartment is a container with a painted back, so an empty box is a surface rather than an absence.
options.risk: The one device that makes it remarkable is the one device the grid cannot tolerate.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.lineage: green-phosphor terminal in a midnight machine room
options.thesis: The whole game as one scrolling typed transcript on curved glass.
options.viewport: 80 columns of green on near-black, the grid drawn in characters, the cursor breathing.
options.case: Loses both axes. This is the category's own stock rebellion — the predictable opposite of the clean white card — and bloom plus afterimage trails over 81 digits that change constantly is legibility noise dressed as atmosphere.
options.kept: System state prints itself as first-class content instead of being parked in chrome.
options.risk: Every device that makes the world feel alive also smears the numerals.

options.label: Versailles Bosquet Vistas
options.lineage: the gardens of Versailles as choreographed axial landscape
options.thesis: Parterres, sightlines and hydraulic sequence as the page's organising system.
options.viewport: Mirrored parterre geometry along one axis, fountains waking in sequence.
options.case: Loses both axes. There is no thread at all between a garden promenade and a logic puzzle, and mirrored symmetry over a grid whose whole point is that no two regions repeat actively misdescribes the task.
options.kept: One governing axis holding an entire composition together so a fixed frame reads as deliberate.
options.risk: Nothing in the world touches the product's mechanism.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The sudoku page every sudoku site ships, executed impeccably: white card, soft shadow, blue selected cell, red conflict.
canonCard.viewport: A centred white card on light grey holding a bordered 9x9, a button row above it and a number pad below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other sudoku page by design — including the one this repo already has.
